top_events.title: Middle East Oil Exports Drop at Least 60% as Hormuz Stays Mostly Closed, Data Shows - EnergyNow.com

analysis.summary: The headline reports Middle East oil exports down at least 60% while the Strait of Hormuz remains mostly closed, indicating a major disruption to global crude flows and materially tighter effective supply.
analysis.why_xom: A sustained supply disruption could lift crude prices, supporting Exxon Mobil’s upstream realizations and earnings, although the headline alone does not quantify XOM-specific exposure or duration.

top_events.title: Brent crude tops $108 as Trump rejects Iranian proposal to reopen Hormuz Strait - CNBC

analysis.summary: Brent crude rose above $108 after Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, indicating continued disruption or uncertainty around a major oil chokepoint.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices can support Exxon Mobil’s upstream revenue and earnings, although the headline provides no details on the duration or operational scope of the Hormuz disruption.

top_events.title: Brent crude tops $108 as Trump rejects Iranian proposal to reopen Hormuz Strait - cnbc.com

analysis.summary: The headline reports that Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was rejected while Brent crude exceeded $108. A continued or unresolved Hormuz disruption implies tighter global crude transit and supports oil prices. The supplied material does not provide further operational details, so the assessment is based on the reported rejection and price reaction.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices can improve Exxon Mobil’s upstream realizations and earnings exposure, although refining and fuel-market effects could offset some benefit. Overall, the reported Hormuz-related supply risk is bullish for XOM.

top_events.title: Shipping Traffic Remains at Virtual Standstill Through Hormuz, Data Shows - EnergyNow

analysis.summary: Reported near-standstill shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz signals a potentially severe disruption to crude and petroleum-product flows, which could support oil prices. The supplied text provides no duration, cause, or confirmed volume impact.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices could benefit Exxon Mobil’s upstream earnings, but impaired Hormuz shipping may also raise logistics costs and disrupt regional supply chains, making the XOM effect mixed rather than unambiguously positive.

proposals.title: Add forward-outcome cohorts for threshold and confirmation events

Only 3 realized exits are available, below the minimum calibration sample.
